recognize_zh: 低倍鐵染色（Prussian blue）的骨髓顆粒中可見大量分支狀藍色含鐵血黃素沉積於巨噬細胞內，表示儲存鐵增加；此倍率無法看到噬血現象本身。
features: Marrow particle with abundant blue, branching hemosiderin deposits within macrophages
Surrounding hemodilute background of red cells
Cellular detail and hemophagocytosis not assessable at this power
describe_en: Low-power Prussian blue-stained bone marrow aspirate smear shows a particle containing abundant coarse, branching blue hemosiderin deposits within macrophages, indicating increased storage iron. Individual cells and hemophagocytosis cannot be evaluated at this magnification. Increased marrow iron stores are a nonspecific finding that can accompany hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis with hyperferritinemia and inflammation-associated iron sequestration.

ddx.vs: Also shows increased macrophage iron with decreased sideroblasts; clinical HLH criteria are needed to separate them.
Iron overload is supported by transfusion history, transferrin saturation and HFE genotype rather than cytopenias with hemophagocytosis.
Sideroblastic anemia is defined by ringed sideroblasts in erythroblasts, which require high-power assessment.
